name: Kanthaswamy
realName: V. Kanthaswamy IPS, Superintendent of Police, CBI Economic Offences Wing
summary: Vikram's 2009 Tamil film hero: a CBI officer who answers wishes left at a Muruga temple while dressed as a rooster-like vigilante, taking black money from the corrupt to help the poor.
origin: Kanthaswamy is the hero of Susi Ganeshan's 2009 Tamil film. By day he is an officer in the CBI's economic offences wing. By night he and his friends read letters left at a Lord Muruga temple by needy people, and he grants their wishes while disguised as an anthropomorphic rooster. He targets rich tycoons hiding black money, and diverts it into funds for the poor. Vikram played the role, and the film is widely described as the first superhero film in Tamil cinema.
powers: Clever tricks to find black money and bank passwords
Backing from a loyal circle of friends

storyline.title: Letters to Muruga
storyline.beat: The hero secretly grants the wishes of people who write letters at a Muruga temple, so locals start believing the god himself is helping them.

storyline.title: Black money found
storyline.beat: During a raid, Kanthaswamy discovers a hoard of black money held by a rich tycoon and starts a game of cat and mouse with the tycoon's daughter.

storyline.title: The bank account trick
storyline.beat: He tricks his way into the tycoon's secret account, moves the money to funds for the poor, and exposes a falsely respected businessman.

storyline.title: A letter in the tree
storyline.beat: The film closes with him finding more wish letters tied to a tree, hinting that the vigilante work will carry on.

quiz.q: What does Kanthaswamy dress as when granting wishes?
quiz.why: He wears an anthropomorphic rooster disguise.

quiz.why: The wish letters are left at a Lord Muruga temple.

theme.tagline: A rooster mask, a temple full of wishes, and a very rich bank account.

timeline.title: Audio launch
timeline.note: The Devi Sri Prasad soundtrack is launched at the Chennai Trade Centre on 17 May 2009, with Vikram singing four of its tracks.

timeline.title: Release
timeline.note: Kanthaswamy opens on 21 August 2009, with the Tamil version given a U certificate.

timeline.title: Telugu version
timeline.note: A Telugu dub called Mallanna follows, with Brahmanandam replacing Vadivelu's comedy in reshot scenes.

timeline.title: Hundred-day run
timeline.note: The film runs for over 100 days in theatres and is described as one of the year's most profitable.

facts.text: The 2007 launch used a laptop-sized electronic invitation made in China with an 8-minute trailer built in. At about Rs 15,000 each, it was called the costliest invite in Indian film history.
After the launch, the team adopted two villages near Madurai, Sangampatti and Gandhi Nagar, for a year, and were said to be the first Tamil production crew to do so.
The villain, tycoon PPP, fakes a stroke to dodge police questions. Later he has a real one when he sees his secret bank account emptied to a zero balance.

Vikram's singing began as rough guide tracks that Devi Sri Prasad asked him to record in Malaysia. The producers liked his voice, so he sang four songs and recorded all four again for the Telugu album.
In the Tamil Kanda Puranam telling of Muruga's battle with the asura Surapadma, the two halves of a split mango tree become a peacock and a rooster, and Muruga takes the rooster as his banner.
Kandaswamy is a form of Muruga's name, and a well-known Jaffna temple, Nallur Kandaswamy, is dedicated to him. The film's hero carries that same name.
Kanthaswamy is called the first superhero film in Tamil cinema: Vikram plays a CBI officer who moonlights as Kokorako, a vigilante dressed as an anthropomorphic rooster.
Veteran actor Raghuvaran was cast as the heroine's father and shot scenes, but he died during production. Ashish Vidyarthi took over the role and the release was pushed back.
In November 2007 a pole on a set at the Chennai Boat Club fell on director Susi Ganeshan's head. He was injured and the shoot paused for a while.
Vikram's page calls Kanthaswamy his most expensive production up to then, beating Anniyan, and notes it had an unusual pre-launch trailer.
In its first week of international release the film took about Rs 37 crore, with roughly Rs 16 crore of that from Tamil Nadu.
The comedian Vivek appeared in the film's first trailer but dropped out. Vadivelu stepped in for the comic role.
Some theatres cut about 15 minutes of Brahmanandam's comedy from the Telugu version, Mallanna.
The tycoon's furious daughter pretends to be in love with Kanthaswamy to take revenge. He sees through it and plays along, until they truly fall for each other.
The crew shot in Italy (where the trailer was filmed), Tanzania, Kenya and Switzerland, then scouted Mexico and filmed a song and several scenes there.
An old Tamil saying holds that wherever there is a hill, there is a temple to Murugan, and most of his temples sit on hillocks.
Hindu tradition describes Muruga's spear, the vel, as a gift from his mother Parvati, and it stands for courage and righteousness.
According to the Skanda Purana, Muruga's birth began as six sparks from Shiva that became six boys raised by the Krittikas, which is why he is called Kartikeya.
Muruga's six best-known temples, the Six Abodes, are at Thiruparankundram, Tiruchendur, Palani, Swamimalai, Tiruttani and Pazhamudircholai, and Sangam literature mentions them.
In the Kanda Puranam telling, Kartikeya first sent messengers to warn the asuras fairly before the war. They ignored the warning.

kidSummary: Kanthaswamy is a police officer who works for the CBI. At night he and his friends dress up as a rooster-like hero and answer wish letters left at a Muruga temple. He finds black money, which is cash hidden from the tax office by the corrupt, and uses it to help people who need it.

story.title: A secret wish-granter
story.text: Kanthaswamy works for the CBI by day and disguises himself as a rooster-like hero when he grants wishes.

story.title: Letters at the temple
story.text: Poor and needy people write their wishes in letters at a Muruga temple, and people start to think the god himself is helping.

story.title: Hidden money
story.text: During a raid he finds a huge pile of black money belonging to a rich tycoon.

story.title: The password trick
story.text: He cleverly tricks the tycoon's daughter into revealing a bank password and moves the money to help the poor.

story.title: More letters
story.text: The film ends with him finding fresh wish letters on a tree and smiling, ready to help again.
